paper.title: Learning What to Say to Your VLA: Mostly Harmless Vision Language Action Model Steering
paper.central_claim: Interactive language-sequence search distilled into a closed-loop LFP plus conformal improvement head steers arbitrary frozen VLAs without original data or fine-tuning, improves sample complexity and ID/OOD success, prevents harmful steering under calibrated perturbations, and elicits recovery not obtained with open-loop prompting.

gap.author_gap: Brittle unintuitive language-to-behavior mapping prevents reliable zero-shot prompting; open-loop language search cannot respond to changed state; harmful edits under shift.
gap.checked_gap: Observed steering harm and composition failures establish real interface/skill-support limits. Learned feedback with abstention is testable; exhaustive novelty not established from author-only related work.

gap.residue: Learn reusable state-dependent prompts plus a reliable do-not-steer rule without VLA weight access, while paying for search and calibration.
gap.stakes: Robot reliability without retraining motor model, with substantial offline robot interaction and slower replanning.
gap.method_response: Narration reduces language search support, execution selection supplies useful command data, RFT makes closed-loop feedback reusable, calibration rejects predicted harm.
gap.remaining_gap: Tie bug in formal guarantee; noisy true-improvement labels; calibrated vs arbitrary OOD; no search-inclusive efficiency comparison; skill support failures.

claims.text: LFP improves frozen-VLA performance and sample complexity with OOD/recovery transfer.
claims.setting: 200 simulation visual-semantic combinations;4 hardware tasks×3 conditions,13 novel sim compositions,2 novel hardware tasks; second VLA separately trained.
claims.baseline/control: Original VLA, direct VLA-LoRA, base VLM, narration SFT; OL/phrase/trajectory search.
claims.selection_vs_test: Training-like search; novel-task holdout; visual/semantic target calibration additional exposure.
claims.result/denominator: 50 sim trials/cell and30 hardware/cell; train base51.2→CP63.8 (+12.6pp,~24.6% relative); hardware nominal50→82.5 (+32.5pp,65% relative).7/13 new compositions zero.
counterevidence: 1000/320 candidate rollouts/task omitted from examples-only sample-complexity comparison.
No isolated low-level skill oracle or matched alternative steering agent; second VLA uses separately trained LFP.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Author-reported closed-loop gains in tested settings and limited task transfer, not total-interaction sample superiority or arbitrary skills.

claims.text: Calibrated refusal guarantees harmlessness and prevents OOD performance degradation.
claims.setting: Empirical harmful label, alpha=.1, target-distribution exchangeable calibration/test.
claims.baseline/control: Always steer vs raw predictor vs calibrated gate;5 random calibration/test splits.
claims.selection_vs_test: 20 calibration examples per perturbation condition; harmful-class threshold fitted on separate target-domain examples.
claims.result/denominator: Reported FPR38.92→9.31% sim,61.11→2.22% hardware; pooled sim success70.93→74.96→75.96 across10000 trials.
counterevidence: Analytical counterexample, our inference not a run: all harmful scores=c, m=20, alpha=.1; k=ceil(21*.9)=19, q=c, s>=q allows every harmful example. FPR=1 under exchangeability. Proof needs strict inequality or valid randomized tie handling, not specified.
Bound concerns empirical-label class FPR, not harm given allow, physical safety, true expected improvement, or arbitrary uncalibrated shifts.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Observed calibrated harmful-class FPR reduction; unrestricted formal guarantee as printed is not established.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Author-reported closed-loop gains over two frozen VLA families in tested sim/physical settings, limited novel-task transfer, and observed calibrated refusal reducing empirically harmful steering. Not universal harmlessness or total-interaction sample superiority.

Independent training repeats, search-inclusive cost and empirical-to-true harm calibration absent.
